Across six framings, including three negation-shaped ones, one candidate dominates: claim `1dcf2bdd...`, "Stable microscopic black holes produced at the LHC would endanger Earth," which is the contrary of the proposed no-risk form. The source text is the conclusion of the LHC safety analysis (Giddings & Mangano style, "no risk of any significance whatsoever"), which asserts exactly that negation. Since a claim and its denial are one node, this is a match with a denied stance; the existing node's direction (the endangerment thesis, affirmative, naming the thing the debate disputes) is the correct canonical direction, so I do not flip it.

input.reasoning: Searched six framings: the proposed canonical form, the source's own wording ("no risk of any significance"), a harmlessness paraphrase, a plain no-risk-at-colliders phrasing, and two explicit negation-shaped framings ("LHC could destroy Earth / doomsday scenario"). The same node dominated every search, peaking at 0.881 under the danger framing. Propositionally, the existing canonical form and the proposed one turn on identical considerations: whether stable, Earth-trapped microscopic black holes from the LHC would accrete and cause harm. Nothing bears on one without bearing on the other; they differ only in polarity, so they are one claim (§2), not a mirror page. The source text asserts the negation of the existing canonical form, hence instance_stance "denies". The existing node's direction is kept rather than flipped to the proposed no-risk wording: the endangerment thesis (the doomsday scenario) is the affirmative form of the question the discourse disputes, and the safety literature, including this source, is organized around denying it; "pose no significant risk" is a negation-shaped form and therefore the poorer direction. The proposed no-risk wording is recorded here as the stance of this instance, with its flavor ("no risk of any significance whatsoever") living in the instance text, not the canonical form.
input.relationship_notes: Supporting structure around the matched claim: 6a7966e4 (stable trapped black hole accretes fast enough to destroy the planet) is the mechanism premise of the endangerment thesis and the main point the source's safety analysis rebuts; d7357393 (white dwarfs and neutron stars exclude dangerous accretion) and dab2fd70 (exclusion holds even without Hawking radiation) are safety-side arguments for the negation; 537e84f7 and 11887800 (cosmic ray collisions above LHC energies without dangerous black holes) likewise support the no-risk side; 44801268 (accretion rate far too low on planetary timescales) is the quantitative subclaim underlying those arguments. Related but distinct: fcab83dc (collider black holes evaporate instantly via Hawking radiation) is a premise of one safety argument, not the risk verdict itself; e382b679 (LHC could produce microscopic black holes under large extra dimensions) is the production premise, orthogonal to danger. Housekeeping for the Curator: 537e84f7 and 11887800 carry identical canonical forms and look like an unmerged duplicate pair.
